WRAP-VS-FLAT TRAP (7th hit in this suite): this capability's guidance explicitly says to wrap the body in a `test_plan` object (claiming a flat body 'is accepted too'). Tested wrapped first, as instructed, since the guidance recommends it: invokeCapability rejected it client-side with 'unknown body: test_plan. accepted: description, end_date, issue_tracker, issues, name, plan_status, start_date, tags' — no HTTP request was ever made. Only the flat form succeeded. DRIFT: the 'wrap is also accepted' half of the guidance does not hold through this tool.

TEST_RUNS SILENT-DISCARD CLAIM: could NOT be verified as documented, and the claim as stated does not hold through this tool. The guidance says a `test_runs` list in the body is 'SILENTLY DISCARDED — 200, plan unchanged, nothing linked, no warning.' In fact test_runs is not even a declared body field on this capability — both rejection messages' 'accepted' list (description, end_date, issue_tracker, issues, name, plan_status, start_date, tags) omits it entirely. Sending test_runs: [] was rejected CLIENT-SIDE by invokeCapability itself before any HTTP call was made: no 200, no silent drop — an explicit, loud 'unknown body: test_runs' error instead. So (1) the call did NOT return 200 with the field silently ignored — it never reached the API at all, and (2) since no write happened, the plan's run linkage was trivially unchanged — confirmed independently anyway via list_test_plan_test_runs before (setup step 2) and after (setup step 4) every write in this probe: exactly one run, TR-9061, throughout. Net effect for a caller of this MCP surface is actually SAFER than documented (a clear rejection beats a silent trap), but it is still DRIFT against the specific documented mechanism ('no warning' is contradicted — there is a very clear warning), and it means the underlying HTTP API's alleged silent-200 behavior is unobservable through invokeCapability for this capability.

Storage verification: the flat update (name/description/tags) returned 200 and a re-read via get_test_plan immediately after confirmed the new values were actually stored (not just echoed) — this half of the contract is a genuine PASS. Response shape matched the declared 'returns' list exactly except for the correctly-absent parent_plan_id (TP-1616 is a top-level plan; the flat returns array lists parent_plan_id unconditionally while the nested schema correctly notes it's sub-plan-only — the same overclaim pattern already seen on sibling capabilities in this batch). No undeclared fields were returned. Overall verdict is DRIFT because of the wrap-guidance contradiction and the test_runs claim mismatch, even though the core rename/description/tag update itself behaved exactly as declared and verifiably landed.
